user.title: GNU+Linux computer
user.description: SSH connection to the computer. The user must be able to become root with sudo (wheel/sudo group) or doas.

password.title: Password
password.description: Password for {user}@{host}. Also used for sudo.

key_file.title: SSH key
key_file.description: Path of the private key inside Home Assistant (e.g. /config/.ssh/...). The sudo password is only needed if sudo asks for one.

generate_key.title: Shared SSH key
generate_key.description:
Add this public key to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` of **{user}** on **{host}**:

`{pubkey}`

For example:

`{command}`

Then press Submit.

power.title: Power actions
power.description:
Which actions may Home Assistant run on this computer? Leave everything off for servers.

Sleep states detected: {detected}.

reauth_confirm.title: Authentication failed
reauth_confirm.description:
**{host}** rejected the credentials of **{user}** (password changed, key removed, or the host key changed). Home Assistant stopped connecting to it.

Enter the new password, the path of a key, or choose *Generate* to use the shared key of Home Assistant — add it to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` first:

`{pubkey}`

Host key now: `{fingerprint}` ({host_key_status}; before: `{old_fingerprint}`). **⚠ ≠ means the host key changed**: submit only if you know why (e.g. the computer was reinstalled).

error.no_sudo: The user cannot become root: add it to the wheel/sudo group, give the sudo password, or allow it in doas.conf (permit nopass)
error.key_rejected: The computer does not accept this key. Add the public key shown above to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the user on the computer, then submit again.
error.password_required: Enter the password, or choose another authentication method.

abort.already_configured: This computer is already configured; connection data updated
abort.wrong_computer: That is a different computer (the machine-id does not match)

data.public_ip: Detect the public IP (the computer asks api.ipify.org)
data.ip_location: Approximate location from the public IP when there is no GPS (asks ipwho.is)

data_description.commands: One per line: `Name = shell command`. Each becomes a button and can be run with the run_command action. Use `$SUDO` to run as root, e.g. `Backup = $SUDO systemctl start backup.service`. Timeout: 5 minutes.

wol_computer.title: Wake-on-LAN through another computer
wol_computer.description: Choose a computer that is always on and in the same network as this one. It will send the magic packet (needs `wakeonlan` or `python3`).

wol_mikrotik.title: Wake-on-LAN through a MikroTik router
wol_mikrotik.description:
The router of this computer's network sends the magic packet with `/tool wol`.

Create a restricted user on the router (RouterOS terminal):

```
{command}
```

The key shown is the one of the path below (by default the shared key of Home Assistant). Leave the password empty to use only the key.

error.not_routeros: Connected, but it does not look like RouterOS
error.invalid_commands: Invalid line: use `Name = command` (name: letters, digits, spaces, up to 40 characters, not repeated)

abort.no_other_computer: There is no other computer configured to act as a relay

options.generate_key: Shared SSH key of Home Assistant (created if missing)

options.computer: Through another computer of this integration

service_control.name: Service control
service_control.description: Start, stop, restart, enable or disable a service on the computer.

command.name: Command
command.description: What to do with the service.

take_screenshot.name: Take screenshot
take_screenshot.description: Takes a screenshot of the active graphical session.

update_log.name: Update log
update_log.description: Returns the output of the last update that ran on the computer.

config_entry_id.name: Computer
config_entry_id.description: Computer to read the log from.

lines.name: Lines
lines.description: Number of lines from the end of the output.

run_command.name: Run custom command
run_command.description: Runs one of the custom commands defined in the options of the computer and returns its output. Administrators only.

command.name: Command
command.description: Name of the command, as written in the options.

use_shared_key.name: Use the shared SSH key
use_shared_key.description: Authorizes the shared key of Home Assistant (/config/.ssh/gnulinux_computer) on the computer with its current credentials, checks that it works and switches to it. Without a computer, does it for all of them. Administrators only.

remove_old_key.name: Remove the old key
remove_old_key.description: Remove from the computer the per-computer key that this integration generated before.
